transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you to see me?

Well, I came in because... I've been having these nights of eating. And when it's over, I just sit there with crumbs and empty containers all around me. I feel so ashamed and disgusted with myself. It's gotten so bad that I can hardly even pray, or look folks at church in the eye the next morning. So, I figured it was time to get some help.
After these eating episodes, do you do anything to try to make up for the food you've eaten, such as making yourself throw up, using laxatives, or fasting?
No, I don't do anything like that. I just... I just sit with it. I don't throw up or take anything, and I don't starve myself the next day. I just feel terrible about it.
During these episodes of eating, do you feel like you've lost control, as if you can't stop eating or control what you're eating?

Yes, that's exactly how it is. Once I take that first bite—usually after the house is quiet for the night—it's like my good sense just steps aside. Even while I'm sitting there telling myself, 'Belinda, stop now,' my hands just keep reaching for more. I really just can't seem to stop myself once it starts.
During these episodes, would you say you eat an amount of food that is definitely much larger than what most people would eat in that same amount of time?

Yes, I would. It's... it's a lot more than anyone else would eat. Like, on a bad night, I can start with a plate of leftover funeral-luncheon casserole. And then, before I even know it, I've eaten that, plus half a pan of brownies, some biscuits, and whatever chicken salad is left in the fridge... all in just one sitting.
About how often do these episodes of eating happen in a typical week?

Well, since my friend passed away, these late-night eating spells have been happening at least once or twice most weeks. And... well, there really hasn't been a month where they've let up at all. It's been pretty constant.
